VI.description: Create a LabVIEW INTERFACE - a .lvclass with no private data control - by calling the project provider's OWN VI\3A Add Interface.lvlib\3AAdd Interface to Project (path).vi. Every input is a string because a helper's controls are set as strings over VI Server\3B the paths are converted on the diagram.\0A\0AWHY A SEPARATE HELPER AND NOT lvai_create_class. The provider VI is an EXACT MIRROR of the class one - measured 2026-08-31 with lvai_vi_terminals against both - with two differences that matter\3A there is NO Parent Class terminal at all\2C because an interface may only inherit from other interfaces\2C and the returned refnum is called Interface rather than Class. NI keeps the two providers in separate libraries (AddInterface\5CSupport next to AddClass\5CSupport\2C same four VIs each)\2C and so do we.\0A\0AAn interface has NO PRIVATE DATA\2C which is the whole definition\3A NI's own manual says an interface 'can be thought of as a class without a private data control'. So there is no carrier VI here and no call to Message Maker.lvlib\3AAdd Member Data to Private Data Control.vi - the two steps that make up most of the class helper. A file written by this helper is distinguishable from a class in exactly one place\2C NI.LVClass.IsInterface = true\2C and by having no Class Private Data item.\0A\0APARENT INTERFACES ARE AN ARRAY\2C and that is the reason this diagram has a loop where the class helper has a constant. Multiple inheritance from interfaces is legal and is the point of the feature - NI's Basic Interfaces example has Flathead inheriting both Rotating Tool and Lever. The caller passes PIPE-separated paths and a COUNT\2C and the count is what the For Loop's N is wired to.\0A\0AWHY A PIPE AND NOT A NEWLINE. Measured 2026-08-31\3A the transport that sets these controls - lvai_run_vi_and_read_values - REFUSES any value containing a line break\2C by name\3A inputContainsNewline\2C because it pairs control names with values BY LINE and a newline in either would shift every later pair onto the wrong control. So a newline-separated list cannot reach this VI at all. A pipe can\3A it is in Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars() on Windows\2C so no real path contains one\2C which makes it a separator that cannot collide with the data. The MCP-facing grammar is still one path per line - a different boundary\2C and the join happens in C#.\0A\0AWHY A COUNT CONTROL AND NOT Array Size. With N wired\2C a count of 0 runs the loop zero times and the indexing output tunnel produces an EMPTY ARRAY\2C which is what Parent Interfaces needs for a root interface. Deriving N from the split array instead would depend on what Spreadsheet String To Array returns for an empty string - if that is one empty element rather than no elements\2C the loop runs once\2C String To Path yields an empty path\2C LVClass.Open fails\2C and Parent Interfaces receives an array holding one INVALID refnum. A conditional output tunnel would also solve it\2C but AIXML's reference records conditional output tunnels as never having been needed and therefore never measured\2C and an unmeasured construct does not belong in a shipped helper. The count is measured ground\3A a wired N plus an auto-indexing input tunnel is the documented For Loop shape.\0A\0AEVERY LVClass.Open REFNUM IS OURS AND IS CLOSED\2C in the second loop\2C and so is the Interface refnum the provider returns at uid 70. That is not tidiness. Measured on the class helper 2026-08-28\3A leaking the refnum a provider returns keeps the new class in LabVIEW's MEMORY past the project close\2C so the next run opens a project listing that class\2C cannot bind the item to the copy already in memory\2C and creates a child with NO PARENT and no error at all. One Close Reference took a two-class run from three LabVIEW restarts to none.\0A\0ATHE CLOSING LOOP TAKES error in FOR ORDERING AND DROPS error out. Without an error wire the loop has no data dependency on the provider call and LabVIEW may run it FIRST\2C closing the parent refnums before they are used. Wiring error in fixes the order\3B consuming error out would turn closing a legitimately invalid refnum - a path that did not open - into a failed run\2C which is Error 1055. Same trick and same reason as uid 88 in lvai_create_class.xml.\0A\0ANEW INTERFACE OWNER STAYS UNWIRED (uid 62\2C an empty refnum)\2C so the interface is NOT added to the .lvproj here and the caller writes that entry itself after closing the project. Carried over from the class helper deliberately\3A measured over nine runs there\2C wiring the owner went from 1 wedge in 4 to 3 wedges in 5. The cause is open\2C the sample is small\2C and it points the wrong way.\0A\0AparentsOpened IS A COUNT OF REFNUMS\2C NOT A VERIFICATION. It says how many entries the loop produced\2C including any that failed to open\2C because merging an error out of a loop costs nodes and answers a question the caller can settle better\3A read the finished .lvclass and count its Parent Libraries entries. The C# side does exactly that\2C which is the same file-first rule the class tool follows after lvai_describe_project reported ok\3A false for a perfectly sound class.
